guides.title: Direct a GTA-style skate line in one continuous shot
guides.desc: Create a 15-second night skate run with grounded board physics, a close chase camera and a reactive trick HUD.

steps.title: 1. Build a line, not a montage
steps.text: Choose one route through the skate spot and keep the camera behind the rider. Continuous geography makes the result feel playable and gives every trick a clear approach and landing.
steps.prompt: Third-person open-world game footage at a wet industrial skate plaza at night. Male skater in a red tracksuit rides toward a low concrete ledge. Close chase camera behind and slightly below shoulder height, city lights reflecting on wet ground, one continuous 16:9 shot.

steps.title: 2. Protect board-to-foot contact
steps.text: The critical failure is feet detaching from the deck. Ask for one ollie and a clean landing, with the board rotating only as much as the body can plausibly control.
steps.prompt: The skater compresses, pops one clean ollie over the ledge and lands with both feet planted over the trucks. Board remains rigid and connected to the rider, wheels contact the ground together, knees absorb impact, no impossible flips or limb distortion.

steps.title: 3. Let the HUD confirm the trick
steps.text: The interface should register the move after landing, not before it. Use a small trick label, score increment and balance meter while keeping the ledge and feet unobstructed.
steps.prompt: Add a restrained game HUD: circular minimap bottom-left, trick name and score top-right, small balance or speed indicator. The score updates immediately after the landing and all UI remains locked to screen coordinates.

steps.title: 4. Cut on the roll-away
steps.text: End after two seconds of stable riding. The roll-away proves the landing; cutting at peak height would hide whether the generated physics actually worked.
steps.prompt: Deliver a 15-second 1920 × 1080 H.264 clip at 24 fps with stereo audio and web fast-start.

guides.result: A readable skate line with one grounded trick, a verified roll-away and game UI timed to the landing.

guides.title: Direct a GTA-style surf stunt with a playable HUD
guides.desc: Build a 15-second open-world surf clip where the wave physics, chase camera and game interface all sell the same playable moment.

steps.title: 1. Frame it like gameplay
steps.text: Use a stable third-person chase camera behind the surfer. A beautiful drone angle would weaken the idea because the clip needs to feel controllable, not observed.
steps.prompt: Third-person open-world game footage of a male surfer riding a turquoise wave through a rocky tropical cove at sunset. Camera follows two metres behind and slightly above the character, wide 16:9 frame, realistic game-engine lighting, continuous shot.

steps.title: 2. Give the wave one readable line
steps.text: The surfer should carve across a single breaking face with a visible spray trail. Do not ask for several tricks—the body mechanics fail when the model has to solve too many direction changes in 15 seconds.
steps.prompt: The surfer shifts weight naturally, cuts across the wave face and throws a clean fan of white spray. Board stays attached to both feet, knees absorb the water movement, wave direction remains consistent and the shoreline advances smoothly.

steps.title: 3. Add HUD elements that react
steps.text: A minimap, speed value and trick score make the shot read as a game only when the numbers respond to motion. Keep them in safe corners and protect the rider silhouette.
steps.prompt: Add a restrained open-world game HUD: circular minimap bottom-left, speed and score bottom-right, small location label top-left. Interface stays sharp and stable while speed and score update during the carve. No large menu panels over the action.

steps.title: 4. Keep the best continuous take
steps.text: Reject takes where the board clips into the water or the HUD swims across the frame. Publish the take with stable feet, one continuous wave and readable interface placement.
steps.prompt: Deliver a 15-second 1920 × 1080 H.264 clip at 24 fps with stereo audio and web fast-start.

guides.result: A compact gameplay-style surf stunt with coherent water motion, chase-camera framing and a HUD that supports the action instead of covering it.

guides.title: Turn a wushu performance into a living ink painting
guides.desc: Direct one 15-second martial-arts shot where the fighter’s movement paints a black ink ring and resolves into a Chinese dragon mural.

steps.title: 1. Lock one visual rule
steps.text: The fighter, floor and background stay monochrome. Only the moving ink changes shape. This prevents the shot from becoming a pile of unrelated effects.
steps.prompt: A cinematic wushu performance inside a vast white ink-wash studio. One female martial artist in a white top and flowing black trousers. Monochrome palette, wet black sumi ink, soft grey mountains in the distance, locked wide camera, realistic fabric and body mechanics.

steps.title: 2. Make movement generate the graphic
steps.text: Tie the ink to the body: the arm sweep pulls a broad brush stroke while the low stance closes it into a circular ring. The effect follows momentum instead of floating independently.
steps.prompt: As she pivots into a low wushu stance, a thick ribbon of wet black ink follows her arms and circles her body. The stroke has visible bristle texture, splatter at direction changes and believable liquid inertia. Keep her face, costume and scale consistent.

steps.title: 3. Resolve the motion into one payoff
steps.text: The final dragon works because it grows from the same ring rather than appearing as a separate cut. Hold the last composition long enough to read the fighter’s scale against the mural.
steps.prompt: The circular ink stroke expands behind the fighter and resolves into a monumental hand-painted Chinese dragon mural. The dragon remains painted ink on paper, not a 3D creature. End on a balanced wide tableau with the fighter centered below it, no text and no camera cut.

steps.title: 4. Remove drift from the final seconds
steps.text: Trim after the dragon composition settles. A clean 15-second arc needs a readable setup, one transformation and a held final image—not another effect after the payoff.
steps.prompt: Export a 15-second 16:9 master. Preserve the original sound design, remove unstable tail frames and encode H.264 with web fast-start.

guides.result: A controlled 15-second art film: one performer, one ink-motion system and one dragon reveal that grows directly from the choreography.

steps.prompt: Close the card with a nav row above a top hairline: a muted borderless "Skip for now" on the left, and on the right an outlined "Back" button plus a dark filled "Continue" button. Under it add a progress line: muted "Step 3 of 4", a 5px rounded track filled 75% in near-black, and "75% complete" on the right.

guides.title: Build a notification inbox with tabs and inline actions
guides.desc: A notification panel with filter tabs, unread markers, day grouping and buttons that resolve the item without leaving.
guides.result: A notification centre that people can actually clear: filter tabs with an unread count, avatar and system rows with quoted context, blue unread dots and tint, inline Retry / Open / Reply actions, day group headers and a footer with mark-all-as-read.

steps.title: Panel shell with filter tabs
steps.text: An inbox needs filters from the start — All, Unread, Mentions and one product-specific tab keep it usable at 24 items.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html on a light grey page (#f6f6f8), system sans-serif, no frameworks. Center a 480px white panel at the top of the page: 16px radius, 1px #e6e6ea border, a soft 0 18px 50px shadow, clipped corners. Inside add a header row with a 16px "Inbox" title, a blue rounded "4 new" count pill and a muted gear glyph pushed to the right. Under it a tab row — All, Unread, Mentions, Publishing — where the active tab is near-black, medium weight, with a 2px underline, sitting on a full-width divider. Make the tabs switch on click.

steps.title: Add the notification rows
steps.text: Two row types cover almost everything: a person with initials, and the system with a branded square. Both keep one meta line.
steps.prompt: Add a scrollable list of rows, each with a 32px round monogram avatar, a 13.2px message with bold names and entities, and a muted 11.5px meta line. Rows: "Mara Reyes requested review on pricing-tiers-billing-toggle" with the quote “Prices look off on the yearly toggle — check the Scale tier.” / "12 minutes ago · Review"; system "Publish failed for admin-data-table-toolbar — media store returned 403." / "40 minutes ago · Publishing"; "Anton K. mentioned you in #renders" with the quote “@you the headless capture is 4× faster, want it on the batch?” / "2 hours ago · Mention"; system "28 renders finished in Client guides — weekly. 9.4 MB total, all under the size limit." / "Yesterday, 02:04 · Renders"; "Tara L. approved kanban-task-board and moved it to Shipped." / "Yesterday, 18:20 · Review". Give the system rows a dark filled avatar with a white Q.

steps.title: Mark what is unread and add inline actions
steps.text: A dot alone is too quiet, a full colour block too loud. Pair a 6px blue dot with a barely-tinted row, then let the row be resolved in place.
steps.prompt: Mark the first four rows unread: a very light blue #f7f9ff background and a 6px blue dot pinned near the left edge of the row. Add inline action buttons under the message for the two rows that need a decision: "Open guide" (dark filled) plus "Reply" on the review request, and "Retry publish" (dark filled) plus "View log" on the failure. Buttons are 8px radius, 12px text.

steps.title: Group by day and close with a footer
steps.text: Date groups on a faint strip give the list a spine, and mark-all-as-read is the one action every inbox owes the user.
steps.prompt: Insert uppercase muted day headers on a #fbfbfc strip: "Today" above the first three rows and "Yesterday" above the last two. Close the panel with a footer on the same tint: a "Mark all as read" link on the left and muted "Showing 5 of 24 · See all" on the right.

guides.title: Build a kanban board with a drag state and WIP limits
guides.desc: Four columns, labelled task cards with progress bars, a lifted card mid-drag and a drop placeholder.
guides.result: A sprint board that reads at a glance: four columns with counts, colour-coded task cards with progress bars and assignee avatars, a WIP-limit warning on the busy column, and a card shown mid-drag with a dashed drop placeholder in the target column.

steps.title: Board header and four empty columns
steps.text: Columns are containers, not cards — a flat grey fill with one border keeps the white task cards readable on top.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html for a kanban board on a light grey page (#f5f5f7), system sans-serif, no frameworks. Header: 22px title "Sprint 24 — Publish pipeline", muted "12 tasks · ends Friday", a right-aligned overlapping avatar stack (AK, MR, TL, +4) and a dark "New task" button. Under it a four-column grid, 14px gap, each column a #eeeef1 panel with 14px radius and a 1px #e2e2e7 border, containing a header with a 13px bold name and a white rounded count pill: Backlog 4, In progress 3, Review 2, Shipped 3.

steps.title: Fill the columns with task cards
steps.text: Cards carry one line of text and nothing else at this stage. If the titles do not read cleanly at 13px, no amount of decoration will save the board.
steps.prompt: Add white task cards (11px radius, 1px border, subtle shadow, 12px padding) with a 13.5px title. Backlog: "Bulk re-publish from the guides ledger", "Empty state for a project with no renders", "Rotate the storage token quarterly". In progress: "Step images 404 when the store is suspended", "Per-step progress frames in every guide", "Card preview falls back to the last frame". Review: "Duplicate guard on the publish runner". Shipped: "Headless batch capture for case pages", "Yearly prices rounded down by a cent". Add a muted 11.5px footer line per card: Est. 3d, Est. 1d, Est. 2h, 2 of 3 checks, Review next, Est. 1d, Waiting on AK, Shipped Tue, Shipped Mon.

steps.title: Add labels, progress bars and assignees
steps.text: Four tinted label colours are enough for a whole board. Pair each with a 4px progress bar so status is readable without opening a card.
steps.prompt: Add a small uppercase label chip on top of every card: red Bug, blue Feature, green Ops, purple UX in soft tinted backgrounds. Under the title add a 4px rounded progress bar on a #ececef track with a near-black fill: 15%, 0%, 0%, 70%, 85%, 40%, 100%, 100%, 100% in card order. Put a 22px round monogram avatar at the right end of each card footer (MR, TL, AK, AK, MR, TL, MR, AK, TL).

steps.title: Show the drag state and the WIP limit
steps.text: A drag needs two halves: the lifted card and the hole it will land in. Rotation plus a deep shadow sells the lift; a dashed block sells the target.
steps.prompt: Show one card being dragged: the second card in "In progress" gets rotate(-2deg) scale(1.02), a near-black border and a heavy 0 18px 40px shadow. In the Review column, above its card, add a dashed drop placeholder — 1.5px #b9b9c2 dashed border, 11px radius, 78px tall, translucent white fill. Add an amber "WIP 3/3" pill to the right of the "In progress" column header to flag the limit.

guides.title: Build a file dropzone with a live upload queue
guides.desc: Idle and drag-over states, per-file progress rows, and the uploaded / failed states with a retry button.
guides.result: An uploader that covers the whole flow: a dashed dropzone that lights up on drag-over, a queue of file rows with type thumbnails, progress bars and status lines, a green completed row, a red over-limit row with Retry, and a footer with totals and actions.

steps.title: Card and the idle dropzone
steps.text: State the limits inside the zone. "Up to 200 MB each" prevents the failure you would otherwise have to design an error for.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html on a light grey page (#f6f6f8), centered, max width 640px, system sans-serif, no frameworks. Add a white card (16px radius, 1px #e6e6ea border, 24px padding) with an 18px heading "Upload render assets" and a muted 13px line "Video, posters and step images for one guide. Compress video to ~8 MB before uploading — the shared store is 1 GB." Under it a dropzone: 1.5px dashed #d3d3da border, 14px radius, #fbfbfc fill, centered content — a 44px rounded icon tile with an upload glyph, a 14.5px bold "Drag files here", a muted line "mp4, webm, mov · jpg, png, webp · up to 200 MB each" and an outlined "Choose files" button.

steps.title: Add the drag-over state
steps.text: Drop targets need an unmistakable hover. Change border colour, background and the icon fill at once, and count the files being dragged.
steps.prompt: Add an active drag state to the dropzone: blue #3b5bfd dashed border, #f3f5ff background, the icon tile filled blue with a white glyph and the headline turned blue and switched to "Drop 3 files to upload", with a 150ms transition. Wire real dragenter/dragover/dragleave/drop handlers that add and remove that state. Show the zone in its active state.

steps.title: Build the upload queue
steps.text: One row per file: type chip, name, size, a 5px progress bar and a status line. That is all people need while bytes move.
steps.prompt: Under the dropzone add a queue of file rows, each a 12px-radius bordered row with a 38px rounded type chip (MP4, PNG, MOV), the file name with a muted size next to it, a 5px rounded progress track with a blue fill, a muted 11.5px status line, and a dismiss ✕ on the right. Rows: final_teaser.mp4 7.8 MB at 92% "Uploading · 92% · 1s left", step_02_result.png 1.2 MB at 64% "Uploading · 64% · 3s left", raw_capture.mov 240 MB at 12% "Queued · waiting for a slot".

steps.title: Finish with success, failure and totals
steps.text: The failed row is the important one: say what went wrong, in the row, and put Retry where the dismiss button was.
steps.prompt: Turn the first row into its completed state: green progress fill, a green tick after the name and the status "Uploaded · stored as guides/pricing/final_teaser.mp4". Turn the third row into a failure: red-tinted border and background, red progress fill, red status "Failed · over the 200 MB limit, compress and retry" and an outlined red "Retry" button instead of the ✕. Close the card with a footer above a hairline: muted "2 of 3 files · 9.0 MB uploaded" on the left, "Cancel all" and a dark "Attach to guide" button on the right.

guides.title: Build a set of empty states with CSS illustrations
guides.desc: Four honest empty states — first run, no results, load failed, no access — plus a compact inline variant.
guides.result: A reusable empty-state kit: one card layout with a pure-CSS stacked-sheets illustration recoloured per situation, specific copy and CTAs for first run, no search results, a failed load with a request id, a permission wall, plus a dashed inline variant for empty sections.

steps.title: One card, honest copy first
steps.text: Write the sentence before the drawing. "No guides published yet" plus a next action beats a clever illustration with vague text.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html on a light grey page (#f6f6f8), centered, max width 1060px, system sans-serif, no frameworks. Add a 21px title "Empty states, four of them" and a muted subline "One layout, four jobs: nothing yet, nothing found, nothing loaded, nothing allowed." Below it a two-column grid holding one white card (15px radius, 1px #e6e6ea border, 26px padding, centered text) with a 15.5px heading "No guides published yet" and a muted 13px line, max 340px wide: "Publish your first case and it lands on the feed in about a minute — media included."

steps.title: Draw the illustration in CSS and add the CTAs
steps.text: No image assets: three rotated rounded rectangles with two grey lines each read as "documents" instantly, and a badge tells you which state it is.
steps.prompt: Above the heading add a 120x78 illustration built only from CSS: three 74x52 rounded sheets stacked and rotated -7deg, 5deg and 0deg, each with two short grey lines inside, the front sheet with a darker border and a soft shadow, plus a 26px dark circular badge with a "+" glyph pinned to the bottom right. Add an uppercase muted "First run" pill above it. Under the text put a centered button row: a dark filled "Publish a guide" and an outlined "Import case.json", then a muted hint line "Or run node publish_case.mjs case.json --dry-run first." with the command in a small code chip.

steps.title: Clone it for no-results and failure
steps.text: Same layout, different colour of badge and different promise. A no-results state must offer a way out; an error state must name the cause.
steps.prompt: Duplicate the card twice, reusing the layout and recolouring only the badge. Second card: pill "No results", blue badge with a magnifier, heading "Nothing matches “comparison”", text "No guide in Interfaces uses that word. Try a broader term or clear the category filter.", buttons "Clear filters" (dark) and "Search all categories", hint "Searched 46 guides across 6 categories." Third card: pill "Load failed", red badge with "!", heading "Could not load your renders", text "The media store answered 403. Your files are safe — this is a token problem, not a data problem.", buttons "Try again" (dark) and "Check status page", hint "Request id req_8f21c0 · retried twice" with the id in a code chip.

steps.title: Add the permission wall and an inline variant
steps.text: Not every empty state deserves a whole card. For an empty section inside a page, a dashed one-line row is enough and keeps the page rhythm.
steps.prompt: Add a fourth card: pill "No access", dark badge, heading "This workspace is private", text "Ask an owner for the Editor role — you will keep your drafts, they just move under the workspace.", buttons "Request access" (dark) and "Back to my workspace", hint "Owners: Mara Reyes, Anton K." Then add a full-width compact variant below the grid: a dashed-border row, left-aligned, with a 40px rounded icon tile, a 14px bold "No steps in this guide yet", a muted line "A guide needs at least one step with a title and an instruction before it can be published." and a right-aligned dark "Add first step" button.

guides.title: Build a ⌘K command palette overlay
guides.desc: A dark floating palette over a dimmed app: grouped results, shortcut hints and a keyboard-active row.
guides.result: A dark command palette that reads like Linear or Raycast: blurred scrim over the host app, a search field with an esc chip, grouped Actions / Recent / Docs results with icons and shortcuts, an active row for keyboard navigation, and a footer with hints and a result count.

steps.title: Fake the host app first
steps.text: A palette only looks like a palette when something sits behind it. A skeleton layout is enough — and it keeps the focus on the overlay.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html on a near-black page (#0b0b0e), light text, system sans-serif, no frameworks. Fill it with a fake app underneath: a top bar with three grey window dots, a muted breadcrumb "Workspace / Renders / June" and a right-aligned bordered chip "Press ⌘K". Under it a two-column skeleton — a 200px sidebar of five short rounded grey bars and a content column of three larger blocks (96px, 220px, 96px) using #1e1e25 fills with #26262d borders.

steps.title: Drop the scrim and the palette shell
steps.text: Scrim plus blur separates layers better than a shadow alone. Centre the card horizontally but pin it near the top — that is where the eye expects a palette.
steps.prompt: Add a full-page scrim rgba(6,6,9,.62) with a 3px backdrop blur, and above it a 620px palette card: background #15151a, 1px #26262d border, 16px radius, a heavy 0 32px 80px rgba(0,0,0,.6) shadow, positioned 96px from the top and horizontally centered. Inside put only the search row: a muted magnifier glyph, a borderless transparent input with placeholder "Search commands, projects, docs…", and a small monospace "esc" key chip on the right, all above a 1px divider.

steps.title: Fill in grouped results
steps.text: Group labels are what make a palette scannable. Keep rows one line each, with the shortcut pushed to the right edge.
steps.prompt: Type "ren" into the input and add a scrollable result list (max height 340px) with uppercase muted group labels. Actions: "Render current shot" ⌘ ⏎, "Duplicate render preset" ⌘ D, "Re-run last prompt" ⌘ R. Recent projects: "Renders / June / teaser-04" 2h ago, "Renders / June / hero-loop" yesterday. Docs: "Rendering: queue and priorities" guide. Every row is a 26px rounded icon tile, a 14px label and a muted right-aligned meta value, with 10px radius on hover.

steps.title: Show the keyboard state and footer
steps.text: The selected row is the whole promise of a palette: hands stay on the keyboard. Make it obvious with a filled icon tile, not just a background.
steps.prompt: Mark the first result as the keyboard-active row: soft #1e1e25 background, 1px inset ring, and an icon tile filled with the accent colour #6d5efc. Add a footer bar above the card's bottom edge with key chips — ↑ ↓ navigate, ⏎ run, ⌘ K toggle — and a right-aligned muted counter "6 of 42 commands".

guides.title: Build an admin table with filters, selection and sorting
guides.desc: An invoices table that behaves: filter chips, row selection with a bulk bar, real sorting and pagination.
guides.result: An admin table you can drop into a real product: search and filter chips, status badges, checkbox selection with a bulk-action bar, a sortable amount column that actually reorders rows, and a pagination footer.

steps.title: Frame the page and the toolbar
steps.text: Tables live inside one card. Build the frame and the controls first — they define the width every column has to live with.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html for an admin screen on a light grey page (#f7f7f8), centered, max width 1120px, system sans-serif, no frameworks. Add a header row: 24px title "Invoices", a 13px muted subline "42 invoices this quarter — 6 need attention." and a right-aligned dark "New invoice" button. Under it a white card with 14px radius and 1px #e7e7ea border containing only a toolbar: a 260px search field with a magnifier and placeholder "Search customer or invoice…", filter chips All / Paid / Due / Failed with All active in dark fill, and a right-aligned muted "Showing 6 of 42".

steps.title: Add the table with real rows
steps.text: Uppercase 11px headers on a faintly tinted strip, tabular numbers on the amount column, and one hairline per row — that is the whole trick.
steps.prompt: Inside the card add a full-width table with columns: checkbox, Invoice, Customer, Status, Amount (right-aligned, tabular-nums), Issued. Header cells are 11.5px uppercase muted on a #fbfbfc strip. Six rows: INV-2041 Northwind Studio billing@northwind.co $1,240.00 12 Jun 2025; INV-2040 Halcyon Labs ap@halcyon.io $480.00 11 Jun 2025; INV-2039 Orbital Retail finance@orbital.com $7,320.00 09 Jun 2025; INV-2038 Kova Interiors hello@kova.design $960.00 07 Jun 2025; INV-2037 Fenwick & Sons accounts@fenwick.uk $2,145.00 05 Jun 2025; INV-2036 Atlas Freight pay@atlasfreight.com $315.00 03 Jun 2025. Render each customer as a 26px round monogram avatar with the company on the first line and the muted email under it.

steps.title: Status badges, checkboxes and the bulk bar
steps.text: Selection needs three signals at once: the checkbox, the tinted row and a bar that names the action. Miss one and users lose the state.
steps.prompt: Add pill status badges with a dot: green Paid, amber "Due in 3 days" / "Due in 9 days", red "Card failed". Put a 15px rounded checkbox in the header and in every row; when checked it fills near-black with a white tick and the row background turns #f7f8ff. Mark two rows selected and add a light indigo bar (#f0f1ff) above the table: a checked box, "2 selected on this page" and right-aligned buttons Send reminder / Export CSV / Mark paid.

steps.title: Make the Amount column sort, add the pager
steps.text: Store the sortable value on the row as a data attribute — the header handler then reorders DOM nodes and never touches formatting.
steps.prompt: Give every row a data-amount attribute and make the Amount header clickable: on click sort rows descending by that value, turn the header text near-black and reveal a ▼ arrow next to it. Show the table already sorted by amount. Add a footer row inside the card: muted "Rows per page: 6" on the left and pagination buttons ‹ 1 2 3 … 7 › on the right, with page 1 as a dark filled square.

guides.title: Design an us-vs-them landing section
guides.desc: Two side-by-side cards that make your workflow look inevitable and the old one look tiring.
guides.result: A conversion-focused comparison section: a solid winning card with check rows and a full-width CTA next to a dashed, muted competitor card. Ships in light and dark with one stylesheet override.

steps.title: Write the header that frames the choice
steps.text: The headline does the persuading; the cards only supply evidence. Two-tone type keeps it from shouting.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html for a marketing comparison section on a light grey page. Add a small pill eyebrow reading COMPARISON, a 38px headline "Built differently, on purpose." where the second half is muted grey, and a 16px muted subline: "Same brief, two workflows. Here is what actually changes for the team shipping the work." Max width 1040px, centered. System sans-serif, no frameworks.

steps.title: Build the winning card
steps.text: Solid background, dark border, real shadow. Visual weight is the argument — the eye lands here first.
steps.prompt: Add a two-column grid with 22px gap. The left card is the winner: white, 20px radius, near-black 1px border and a soft elevated shadow. Inside: a black pill badge "✓ With Quadcode", a 20px heading "One workspace, end to end", a muted caption, and five list rows. Each row is a 22px black circle with a white check plus a 15px line of text, separated by 1px hairlines, no line under the last row.

steps.title: Build the losing card and the CTA
steps.text: Dashed border, no shadow, grey icons. Never make the competitor card ugly — make it quiet.
steps.prompt: The right card is the competitor: transparent background, dashed 1px border, no shadow. Grey pill badge "✕ The usual way", heading "Five tools, five exports", muted caption, and five rows mirroring the winner's rows one for one, each with a light grey circle, grey cross and muted text. Back in the left card, add a full-width dark CTA button "Start your first case" with a 12px radius and a tiny centered note under it: "No credit card. Ships in minutes."

steps.title: Add a dark variant
steps.text: Invert the tokens rather than the whole design: the winner card keeps its weight by staying the lightest surface on the page.
steps.prompt: Add a dark variant by overriding only the tokens: page #08080a, cards #111114, borders #26262b, text #fafafa, muted #8b8b93. Invert the winning card accents — white badge with dark text, white check circles, white CTA with dark label — and keep the competitor card dashed and dim. Screenshot both the light and the dark variant at 1440px wide.

guides.title: Build a tabbed platform comparison block
guides.desc: One comparison panel, three competitor tabs, all driven from a single data array.
guides.result: A light, marketing-ready comparison panel. Pill tabs switch the rival, the capability rows and the score line re-render from data, and adding a fourth competitor is one object in an array.

steps.title: Model the data before the markup
steps.text: Everything on screen is derived from one array. Get that shape right and the UI writes itself.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html for a "Compare design platforms" section. Define the content as one JavaScript array called RIVALS. Each entry has: id, name, brand colour, a one or two letter logo mark, and a rows array of [capability, our answer, their answer] triples. Seed it with three rivals — Figma, Canva and Framer — four capability rows each. Light theme, system sans-serif stack, no frameworks and no CDN.

steps.title: Render pill tabs from the array
steps.text: Tabs are buttons with aria-selected, not divs. You get keyboard and screen-reader support for free.
steps.prompt: Render one pill tab per rival, labelled "Quadcode vs <name>", each with a small dot in the rival brand colour. Use real buttons with role="tab" and aria-selected. The active tab is filled near-black with white text; the inactive tabs are white with a 1px border and muted text, and lighten their border on hover. Clicking a tab sets the active index and re-renders the panel.

steps.title: Lay out the three-column panel
steps.text: A CSS grid with the same 1.3fr 1fr 1fr template on the header and on every row keeps the columns locked together without a table element.
steps.prompt: Below the tabs add a white panel, 18px radius, 1px border, soft shadow. Header grid of 1.3fr 1fr 1fr: the label "Capability", then our brand with a black rounded logo mark, then the rival with its own coloured mark. Each capability row uses the identical grid template: muted label, our answer with a green check prefix in medium weight, their answer with a grey cross prefix in muted colour. Separate rows with 1px borders, no border on the last row.

steps.title: Add the score footer and verify every tab
steps.text: The footer closes the argument and gives the CTA somewhere to live. Then click through all tabs and check nothing shifts.
steps.prompt: Add a tinted footer inside the panel with a generated line "Quadcode wins N of N capabilities vs <rival>" on the left and a solid dark "Start free" button on the right. Then switch through every tab and confirm the panel height and column widths stay stable, no text wraps awkwardly, and the rival logo colour updates correctly. Screenshot the first and the last tab at 1440px wide.

guides.title: Build a pros and cons review block
guides.desc: A balanced two-column block that argues both sides of one option and ends with a verdict.
guides.result: A reusable review block: a green pros column, a red cons column with matching row counts, and a scored verdict card underneath. Swaps to a neutral editorial palette with a four-token override.

steps.title: Set the editorial header
steps.text: Pros and cons only work when the reader knows what is being judged. Kicker, title, one line of context — nothing more.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html with a pros and cons review block on a white page, max width 920px, centered. Header: an uppercase muted kicker "HONEST REVIEW", a 30px title "AI-generated video for social ads", and one muted 15px line: "One option, both sides of it. Read the trade-offs before you commit a campaign budget." System sans-serif, no frameworks, no CDN.

steps.title: Build the two tinted columns
steps.text: Same padding, same radius, same number of rows on both sides. Any imbalance reads as bias.
steps.prompt: Add a two-column grid with a 20px gap. Left box: very light green background, light green border, 16px radius, a bold green header row with a rounded green chip containing a plus sign and the label Pros. Right box: very light red background, light red border, same radius, bold red header with a red chip containing a minus sign and the label Cons. Give each box exactly four list rows: an 18px filled circle marker (check on the left, cross on the right) plus 15px text at 1.55 line height, 14px gap between rows.

steps.title: Write honest content, not marketing
steps.text: Concrete numbers beat adjectives. Name the real weak spots — that is what makes the pros credible.
steps.prompt: Fill the block with honest content about AI-generated video for social ads. Pros: a finished 15-second cut in under an hour, ten variants for the price of one shoot, no crew or location dependencies, same-day iteration from campaign feedback. Cons: faces and hands need a human pass, product geometry drifts between shots, takes over 10 seconds lose temporal consistency, licensing rules differ per model. Keep every line under about 70 characters and use plain English.

steps.title: Add the verdict and a neutral variant
steps.text: The verdict card is what people screenshot. Then prove the block survives a palette where colour cannot carry the meaning.
steps.prompt: Under the grid add a verdict card: 1px light border, 14px radius, a dark rounded score badge reading "8.5 / 10" on the left, then a bold "Verdict" label and a two-line muted summary. Then produce a neutral editorial variant by overriding only four tokens so both boxes become light grey with the cons box keeping a dashed border — the icons and labels must still make the pros and cons obvious without colour. Screenshot both variants at 1440px wide.

guides.title: Build a comparison table with row selection
guides.desc: A dark-first data table where every row can be toggled into a comparison set with one click.
guides.result: A self-contained page with a searchable, filterable comparison table. Each row toggles between Compare and a red Remove state, the footer counts the current selection, and the whole thing works in both dark and light themes.

steps.title: Describe the component and its data
steps.text: Start a new page and let the agent scaffold the markup, the design tokens and the sample dataset in one pass. Keep every colour behind a CSS variable so the theme switch later costs nothing.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html file with a product comparison table. Dark theme by default, all colours defined as CSS variables on :root plus a light override on html[data-theme="light"]. Card container: 980px max width, 16px radius, 1px border, soft shadow, centered on the page. Inside: a title "Comparison Table", a toolbar with a search input, a category select and a Reset button, then a table with columns Category, Price ($), Rating, Stock, Select. Seed it with 6 rows of demo products (laptops, tablets, smartphone, monitor). No frameworks, no CDN, plain HTML, CSS and JS only.

steps.title: Add the Compare / Remove toggle
steps.text: The whole point of the component is the toggle. Keep the selection in a Set, re-render the rows from state, and make the selected state impossible to miss.
steps.prompt: Add row selection. Keep selected row indexes in a JavaScript Set and re-render the table body from that state. An unselected row shows an outline button labelled Compare. A selected row shows a bold red destructive button labelled Remove, white text, and the row itself gets a subtle red background tint. Clicking the button toggles the row. Update a footer line to read "N of 6 rows selected" and swap a hint pill between "Pick 2+ rows to compare" and "Ready — compare side by side".

steps.title: Wire search, filter and reset
steps.text: Filtering must never lose the selection — that is the detail most implementations get wrong. Filter the view, not the state.
steps.prompt: Wire the toolbar. The search input filters rows by category name, case insensitive. The select filters by exact category with an All option. The Reset button clears the search, sets the select back to All and clears every selected row. Important: filtering must only change which rows are visible, it must never drop rows that are already selected. Re-render on every input and change event.

steps.title: Check both themes and ship
steps.text: Flip the theme attribute and screenshot both states. If the red destructive button still reads clearly on white, the token set is correct.
steps.prompt: Verify the light theme by setting document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'light'. Check contrast of the destructive Remove button, the muted footer text and the row tint on the light background. Fix any token that drops below comfortable contrast, then export a screenshot of both the dark and the light state at 1440px wide.

guides.title: Make an 8-bit us-vs-them CTA block
guides.desc: A retro pixel card with a three-column feature table and a chunky Press Start button.
guides.result: A pixel-perfect retro comparison CTA: hard 8-bit borders built from box-shadows, a Press Start 2P headline, six us-vs-them rows and a start button that presses down on click. Recolours to any CRT palette by changing two variables.

steps.title: Build the pixel frame
steps.text: The 8-bit look is all in the border. Never use border-radius; stack four hard box-shadows instead so the corners stay square and the edge reads as pixels.
steps.prompt: Create a single self-contained index.html for a retro 8-bit CTA card. Load the Press Start 2P font from Google Fonts with a monospace fallback. Background near-black, card slightly lighter. Build the card border WITHOUT border-radius: use four hard box-shadows (0 -6px, 0 6px, -6px 0, 6px 0, all spread 0) in the foreground colour plus one 6px outline in the card colour, so the frame looks like a stepped pixel border. Card max width 940px, generous padding, centered vertically and horizontally. No frameworks.

steps.title: Add the comparison table
steps.text: Three columns: feature, us, them. Keep the type tiny — a 10px pixel font reads bigger than it measures.
steps.prompt: Inside the card add a headline "WHY_US?" in the pixel font, a small dim subline "LEVEL UP YOUR STACK" with a blinking underscore animated in steps(1), and a three-column table: FEATURE, 8BIT UI, OTHERS. Six rows: vector icons, customizable, dependencies, dark mode, pixel borders, free forever. Our column is green and prefixed with +, the competitor column is dim grey and prefixed with -. Header underlined with a 4px solid rule, rows separated by 2px dashed lines. Font size 10px, line height 1.9, letter spacing 1px.

steps.title: Ship the chunky CTA button
steps.text: Same box-shadow trick as the frame, plus a 4px downward nudge on :active — that tiny travel is what sells the arcade feel.
steps.prompt: Add a centered call-to-action button labelled "PRESS START >". Same pixel border technique as the card but in the dark ink colour, green fill, dark text, no border-radius, 18px by 34px padding, font size 11px. On :active translate it 4px down with a 60ms transition so it feels like a physical arcade key.

steps.title: Reskin it to an amber CRT
steps.text: Because every colour lives in a variable, a whole new arcade palette is a two-line change. Great for A/B testing a landing page.
steps.prompt: Recolour the whole block to an amber CRT palette by overriding only the CSS variables: accent and border become #fbbf24, page background #140f02, card #1b1403. Keep the competitor column dim grey. Confirm the pixel border and the button shadow still read correctly against the warm background, then screenshot the variant at 1440px wide.

guides.title: SNAP/01 — Parametric Kitchen Configurator: from Form Logic to 3D Module Library
guides.desc: A complete Senior product-design pipeline for a real-time kitchen configurator: input/live-preview wireframe logic, a weighted decision matrix for the snapping model, a flagship identity render, a locked-dimension module library, and 6 production GLB meshes rebuilt from photoreal studio references after root-causing two Meshy defects.

steps.title: 1. Lock the input-to-preview wireframe logic
steps.text: Two-panel blueprint: a width/depth/height input form on the left, a live floor-plan preview on the right, connected by a "LIVE SYNC" link so every field edit redraws the plan immediately — no separate "Generate" button, no round-trip.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Two-panel wireframe sheet — input form (left) driving a live floor-plan preview (right), orange dimension arrows, explicit LIVE SYNC connector between the two panels.

steps.title: 2. Score the snapping model with a weighted matrix
steps.text: Three snapping strategies scored on Trust (35%), Speed (20%), Error Rate (30%), Build Cost (15%): Grid-Snap 4.50, Rigid Presets 4.35, Freeform 2.50. Grid-Snap wins by only 0.15 over Rigid Presets — close enough that the rule gets written down, not left to memory: grid pitch = width of the narrowest module.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Decision-matrix sheet comparing Grid-Snap / Freeform / Rigid Presets against 4 weighted criteria, with floor-plan icon per strategy and a locked scoring rule footer.

steps.title: 3. Render the flagship identity kitchen
steps.text: One L-shaped run + island, on a neutral graphite studio backdrop, with the material palette locked before any single module gets modeled: OAK #C08A52 for fronts, GRAPHITE #22262B for worktops, STEEL #9AA3AC for hardware. Six modules visible and separable in one shot: base run, wall run, corner unit, appliance tower, island, hood.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Flagship L-kitchen + island identity render, neutral graphite studio background, OAK/GRAPHITE/STEEL material palette, all 6 module types clearly separable.

steps.title: 4. Define the module library on a locked grid pitch
steps.text: Six modules, one 300mm grid: Base Cabinet 600×600×720, Wall Cabinet 600×350×720, Drawer Stack 300×600×720 (the narrowest — sets the pitch), Corner Unit 900×900×720, Island 1800×900×900, Appliance Bay 600×600×2100. Every width is a multiple of 300mm, so any two modules snap edge-to-edge with zero gap or overlap.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Orthographic module-library sheet, 3×2 grid, 6 kitchen modules with dimension lines and W×D×H spec line each, same OAK/GRAPHITE/STEEL palette as the identity render.

steps.title: 5. Rebuild all 6 modules as production GLB meshes
steps.text: First pass fed the flat schematic icons straight into Meshy — result: phantom drawer-front seams and no depth cues. Fix: 6 dedicated photoreal studio references (same palette, same background) generated first, then meshed. Two defects still slipped through — a corner unit reading its "diagonal-face door" as a literal barn-door Z-brace, and a base cabinet growing tiny metal legs no prompt asked for. Root-cause fix for both is in the prompts below, not in the mesh: reworded the corner reference to "one angled corner facet, plain flat door, no Z-brace," and the base cabinet to "flush plinth base, zero gap to floor." Both regenerated clean on the next pass.
steps.prompt: GOAL: 6 individual production GLB meshes (quad topology, ENABLE_PBR) built from 6 photoreal single-module studio references, matching the step-3 identity render palette and the step-4 locked dimensions exactly.

steps.title: 6. Build the real configurator — hand-coded, not generated
steps.text: ~300 lines of plain HTML/CSS/JS, no framework: a 6-item drag palette, a 300mm-pitch grid canvas (44px per cell — same pitch step 2 locked), a live BOM panel, and a 3D inspector reusing the exact 6 GLB files from step 5. Collision check is an AABB scan against an occupied-cell hash set; Corner Unit is only accepted if its 3×3-cell footprint lines up with one of the 4 room corners — 4 boolean comparisons, not a general polygon test, because a rectangular room only has 4 corners.

steps.title: 7. Ship it live — drag, snap and orbit right here
steps.text: Not a screen recording — the actual widget, embedded live below via iframe, running the same JS that produced the step-6 screenshot. Drag Corner Unit into a corner, drag Island into the open floor, then click any placed piece to orbit it in 3D. Resize the room and modules that no longer fit get dropped automatically.

steps.title: 8. Technical spec — BOM, pricing formula, collision rules
steps.text: BOM fields: module name, quantity, unit price, line total. Formula: Total = Σ(unit price × qty) × 1.08 — the 8% hardware/install fee is a visible multiplier, not a hidden markup. Prices locked per module: Base Cabinet €420, Wall Cabinet €260, Drawer Stack €340, Corner Unit €610, Island €1,450, Appliance Bay €890. Collision rule: zero clearance by design — the grid pitch already equals the narrowest module, so edge-to-edge snapping needs no gap. Corner rule: Corner Unit valid only at the 4 room-corner cells.

guides.result: A locked 300mm-pitch module library (6 GLB meshes, all snap-compatible edge-to-edge), the 4 concept sheets that justify every dimension and interaction rule, and a real hand-coded configurator widget — drag-and-drop grid placement, live 3D inspection and a live-computed BOM — embedded and playable directly in this guide.

guides.title: NPC/01 — Design a Dark-Fantasy Deceiver: from Silhouette to 3D Handoff
guides.desc: A complete Senior Gamedev pipeline for an original dark-fantasy NPC (The Court Parasite): silhouette readability test, weighted score matrix, identity render, 4-view turnaround, FACS expressions, animation poses, interactive 3D GLB model, and technical A-pose socket spec.

steps.title: 1. Force three distinct silhouette massings
steps.text: Start with pure black shapes at 1:1 scale before any face or costume work. Variant A (Wing Collar), B (Relic Chain) and C (Moth Cloak) each test a different C-curve and collar height. If a silhouette does not read at 120 px, it is dead — no render saves it.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Generate 3 distinct black silhouette massings for a dark-fantasy diplomat NPC. A: high bat-wing collar, hands hidden. B: heavy relic chain weighting the torso forward. C: moth-cloak shoulders dissolving into the coat. Pure black on light grey, 1:1, no faces, no costume detail. Judge only readability at small size.

steps.title: 2. Score variants with a weighted decision matrix
steps.text: Score every silhouette against Authority (30%), Threat (25%), Magic (20%), Readability at 120px (15%), Mobility (10%). Variant A wins at 4.25 weighted — the bat-wing collar is locked by numbers, not taste. This sheet is what you show a client when they ask "why this one".
steps.prompt: GOAL: Senior game-concept decision sheet. Score the 3 silhouettes from step 1 against 5 weighted criteria (Authority 30, Threat 25, Magic 20, Readability 15, Mobility 10). Show per-criterion scores, weighted totals, and a verdict row declaring the winner. Swiss editorial layout, dark ink on bone paper.

steps.title: 3. Lock face, materials and palette in the identity render
steps.text: Render the canonical 3/4 full-body anchor. Palette lock: VOID #120F17, BLOOD #4A1830, BONE #C7B79B, STEEL #8A9199. High stiffened collar, concealed hands, signet cane. Every later sheet must match this render — it is the single source of truth.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Full-body identity render for THE COURT PARASITE using silhouette A. 3/4 view, high stiffened wing collar hiding the jaw, long sleeves concealing hands, signet cane. Palette: void black #120F17 coat, dried-blood #4A1830 lining, bone #C7B79B face, steel #8A9199 accents. Flat neutral backdrop, concept-art finish.

steps.title: 4. Produce the orthographic 4-view turnaround
steps.text: FRONT / 3-4 / SIDE / BACK locked to the identity render on warm bone paper (#EDE8DF). The back view designs the collar rear plane without inventing a cape. Modelers build from this sheet — proportions here are law.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Production turnaround sheet, 4 orthographic views (FRONT, 3/4, SIDE, BACK) of THE COURT PARASITE on warm bone paper #EDE8DF. Keep proportions identical across views, match the identity render palette and collar geometry. Clean line art with flat color fills, labeled view headers.

steps.title: 5. Map expression range and prop logic
steps.text: Six facial states (Neutral Court, Polite Smile, Predator Focus, Dialogue Tell, Spell Whisper, Mask Crack) plus 4 functional callouts: Wing Collar, Void Coat, Signet Cane, Court Ring. Animators and dialogue writers work from this sheet.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Expression + accessory sheet. 6 head portraits of THE COURT PARASITE (Neutral Court, Polite Smile, Predator Focus, Dialogue Tell, Spell Whisper, Mask Crack) and 4 clean accessory callout panels (Wing Collar, Void Coat, Signet Cane, Court Ring). Keep the identity render face model consistent across all states.

steps.title: 6. Define the key animation start poses
steps.text: Four readable full-body start poses: 01 Idle, 02 Dialogue Tell, 03 Spell Cue, 04 Attack Anticipation. Each preserves the silhouette — no generic action-hero spread. These are the first frames animators key from.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Animation handoff sheet with 4 key start poses (Idle, Dialogue Tell, Spell Cue, Attack Anticipation). Full body, same model and palette as the identity render. Poses must read as silhouettes and avoid superhero tropes — this character threatens with stillness.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the production 3D model — drag to orbit
steps.text: The GLB mesh generated from the concept stack (35k tris budget). Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom. Check the collar volume from behind and the sleeve drape from the side — the two spots where 2D-to-3D translations usually break.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Generate a production 3D character mesh from the locked identity render and turnaround. Budget 35k triangles, A-pose, watertight, ready for retopo and rigging. Export GLB.

steps.title: 8. Spec the technical A-pose, sockets and FACS targets
steps.text: The rigging contract: 45° A-pose blueprint with engine sockets (socket_hand_r, socket_collar_vfx, socket_ring_l, root_ground), 68-joint skeleton, 35k tris budget, 1024 px/m texel density, and FACS facial targets (AU1, AU2, AU4, AU12, AU15, AU25). This sheet ends design arguments — everything is measurable.
steps.prompt: GOAL: Technical 3D rigging sheet in orthographic A-pose (45° arms). Annotate engine sockets (socket_hand_r, socket_collar_vfx, socket_ring_l, root_ground), joint count 68, poly budget 35k tris, texel density 1024 px/m, FACS targets AU1 AU2 AU4 AU12 AU15 AU25. Blueprint style, precise callouts, no decoration.

guides.result: Full production-grade character bible for an original dark-fantasy NPC: 6 concept sheets, an inspectable 3D GLB mesh (35k tris), and a technical A-pose socket + FACS specification ready for engine handoff.

guides.title: SAVOR/01 — The Evidence of Food: a 20-second motion identity from six stills
guides.desc: Turn scattered food evidence — receipts, printed dates, barcodes, notes — into a typographic decision system: USE FIRST / USE SOON / STABLE / CHECK. Six GPT-Image keyframes, one controlled 20-second sequence, zero fake freshness scores.

steps.title: 1. Define what the system refuses to do
steps.text: Start with the negative brief, not the moodboard. SAVOR/01 never detects freshness, never labels food safe or unsafe, and never replaces package guidance. That constraint is the entire concept: the system organizes evidence the user already has — receipts, printed dates, opened dates, storage zones — instead of inventing an AI verdict. Write four plain-language states before touching visuals: USE FIRST, USE SOON, STABLE, CHECK.
steps.prompt: Lock the safety rule: this system organizes known information. It never claims to analyze food, never outputs a score, never uses medical or danger iconography. Every status must be readable as text + shape + color, so meaning never depends on color alone.

steps.title: 2. Spill the evidence with physical inertia
steps.text: The opening is chaos on purpose: receipt fragments, barcode stripes, printed dates and halftone food crops enter from the frame edges at different speeds with slight rotational overshoot. The SAVOR/01 lockup stays dead still at center while the mess moves around it — the contrast between a fixed identity and uncontrolled evidence is the hook.
steps.prompt: Editorial collage frame, warm paper background #F2EEE5, near-black ink typography. Scattered food evidence fragments: thermal receipt strips with torn edges, barcode sections, printed date stamps, opened-product notes, halftone food photography crops. Fragments enter from frame edges with varied rotation and overlap, physically scattered not decoratively arranged. A small fixed typographic lockup 'SAVOR/01' holds still at the center. Condensed grotesk display type, tabular numerals, registration marks. 16:9, 1920x1080. No UI mockups, no app screens, no people, no gradients.

steps.title: 3. Make conflicting dates break the grid
steps.text: Food date language is genuinely broken: USE BY, BEST BEFORE, OPENED and purchase dates contradict each other in real kitchens. Show it as a typographic collision — one giant black date, three competing labels sliding and rotating into it, an 8-frame hold on the impact. This is the 'why' of the whole system in 3 seconds.
steps.prompt: Editorial typographic frame on warm paper #F2EEE5. One massive black date '21 JUN' in condensed grotesk dominates the grid. Three conflicting date labels collide with it: 'USE BY' sliding left to right, 'OPENED' rolling downward, 'BEST BEFORE' rotated 7 degrees into the collision. Ink texture like rubber date stamps, hard overlaps, registration marks at edges, barcode shutter closing from the sides. Near-black ink #20201E, tomato accent #C6382C. 16:9, 1920x1080. English text only, no UI, no icons, no people.

steps.title: 4. Register evidence with OCR logic
steps.text: The system earns trust by showing what it reads. Six registration boxes draw on clockwise around a yoghurt crop — product name, use-by date, opened date, storage zone, quantity — and each box overshoots its target by a few pixels before snapping into place. The seventh box says NO SAFETY VERDICT and stays neutral black: the system states its own limit inside the design.
steps.prompt: Editorial evidence-capture frame on warm paper. One halftone yoghurt cup crop at center, surrounded by six precise registration boxes drawn in near-black ink: PRODUCT, USE BY, OPENED, STORAGE, QTY, and a final neutral box reading 'NO SAFETY VERDICT'. Boxes have thin rule lines, corner ticks, small tabular metadata labels, OCR-style alignment marks. Dry scanner aesthetic, condensed grotesk labels, cobalt accent #1755A5 for active registration. 16:9, 1920x1080. No glossy UI, no holograms, no scan beams, no people.

steps.title: 5. Sort by position first, color second
steps.text: Exactly 12 evidence tiles enter from scattered positions and reorganize into four horizontal lanes. The motion rule matters: tiles sort by vertical position first, and status color appears only 4 frames later. Priority is expressed as physical order — color is a label, not the mechanism. Three tiles per lane, short stagger, small recoil at the settle point.
steps.prompt: Editorial system frame on warm paper, 12-column grid. Twelve evidence tiles — receipt fragments, date stamps, barcode pieces, food crops with metadata labels — reorganizing into four horizontal lanes. Lane headers in condensed grotesk: USE FIRST (tomato #C6382C), USE SOON (amber #C68A24), STABLE (cool grey #9A9B96), CHECK (cobalt #1755A5). Tiles mid-sort with visible position logic, tabular numerals, registration ticks. 16:9, 1920x1080. No app UI, no rounded cards, no drop shadows, no people.

steps.title: 6. Build the four-state typographic system
steps.text: The payoff frame: four vertical fields, one per state. Each state is text + shape + color — circle for USE FIRST, triangle for USE SOON, equals sign for STABLE, diagonal X for CHECK. Never a medical plus, never color alone. Words reveal bottom-to-top through hard masks; symbols stamp in like print cylinders. This single frame is the whole product.
steps.prompt: Editorial typographic system frame on warm paper #F2EEE5. Four equal vertical fields separated by hairline rules. Each field shows one food-triage state in condensed grotesk: USE FIRST with a circle in tomato #C6382C, USE SOON with a triangle in amber #C68A24, STABLE with an equals sign in cool grey #9A9B96, CHECK with a diagonal X in cobalt #1755A5. Symbols read as stamped print marks, small metadata labels under each state, tabular numerals. 16:9, 1920x1080. English only, no icons beyond the four symbols, no UI, no people, no gradients.

steps.title: 7. Collapse everything into one lockup
steps.text: The finale is compression: the four fields fold into a single horizontal evidence strip, the barcode travels to center and stops dead, the four symbols reorder into one row. SAVOR/01 resolves with a 2-frame red misregistration before alignment — a small print-imperfection detail that makes the system feel physical, not rendered. Hold the final frame long enough to read.
steps.prompt: Editorial final-lockup frame on warm paper #F2EEE5. One horizontal evidence strip across the center combining receipt texture, barcode section and date stamps. Above it the condensed grotesk lockup 'SAVOR/01' in near-black ink with a subtle red misregistration offset, below it the line 'THE EVIDENCE OF FOOD'. The four state symbols — circle, triangle, equals, diagonal X — in one ordered row with their state colors. Registration marks at the corners, generous negative space. 16:9, 1920x1080. English only, no UI, no people.

steps.title: 8. Animate with sound as the timing layer
steps.text: The 20-second cut runs 00–03 spill, 03–06 collision, 06–09 capture, 09–13 triage, 13–17 states, 17–20 lockup at 24 fps. Sound is dry foley, not music: paper feed, scanner ticks, three stamp impacts, six optical clicks, four print-cylinder hits, one low tonal pulse at the lockup. A calm English voiceover explains the logic in three sentences — the system organizes evidence instead of inventing a score. Add the brand watermark at 10% frame width, centered, flush to the bottom edge.

guides.result: A complete 20-second motion identity: six GPT-Image keyframes on one warm-paper grid, a four-state typographic triage system (USE FIRST / USE SOON / STABLE / CHECK), dry foley sound design and a calm English voiceover. The system organizes food evidence the user already has — it never claims to detect freshness or safety.

guides.title: Building Autopsy: Convert an Abandoned Factory into a Boutique Hotel
guides.desc: Turn one 1912 textile factory into a 42-key boutique hotel without letting the plans, section and final render contradict each other.

steps.title: 1. Fix the facts before making a gesture
steps.text: Start with one measured base file. If the grid moves now, every later view will contradict it.
steps.prompt: Create a concept-level measured as-built plan for a fictional 1912 textile factory. Footprint: 54.0 m × 24.0 m. Grid: 6 bays at 9.0 m in the long direction and 4 bays at 6.0 m in the short direction. Keep the brick perimeter, every cast-iron column, and two existing stairs in opposite corners. Draw as a precise architectural survey sheet, not a mood board. Include grid labels 1–7 and A–E, a north arrow, dimensions, and a 1:200 scale bar.

steps.title: 2. Make removal specific
steps.text: The void is one measured cut, not a vague instruction to open the centre.
steps.prompt: From the 54 × 24 m as-built plan, create a keep/remove/add intervention diagram. KEEP: brick perimeter, cast-iron grid, end stairs and all atrium-edge columns. REMOVE: floor plates at levels +4.50 and +9.00 plus roof directly over bays 3–4 / B–C; remove only the column at grid 4/C. ADD: a bronze independent frame around the 18.0 × 12.0 m void, two glass lifts, 2.0 m galleries and a roof lantern set back 1.5 m from the roof cut. Use charcoal for keep, coral hatch for remove, mint and bronze for add. Give every operation a clear legend.

steps.title: 3. Program the ground floor around the void
steps.text: Public life belongs at ground level. Service stays in one corner; the atrium stays a public room.
steps.prompt: Create a proposed ground-floor plan for the factory hotel using the fixed 6 × 4 grid. Keep the 18.0 × 12.0 m atrium at bays 3–4 / B–C empty above ground level. Place reception and entry south-west; restaurant and kitchen north-east; back-of-house and staff south-east; two accessible rooms north-west; two retained stairs in opposite corners. Place a lounge bar and two glass lifts inside the atrium perimeter, without turning the void into enclosed rooms. Show the grid, program labels and a short note explaining circulation.

steps.title: 4. Stack keys without invading the atrium
steps.text: Each upper floor holds 20 keys while keeping the opening and a 2.0 m gallery loop intact.
steps.prompt: Create a typical upper-floor plan for levels +4.50 and +9.00 using the exact same 54 × 24 m grid and 18 × 12 m atrium void. Place 20 keys on each floor: 10 north-facing rooms, 10 south-facing rooms, with housekeeping and one suite at the east end. Keep the two existing stairs. Add a 2.0 m gallery all around the void. No room, bathroom or service enclosure may enter the atrium. Show level labels, grid, gallery width and room count.

steps.title: 5. Use a section to prove the spatial claim
steps.text: A plan can hide impossible ideas. The section has to prove the lantern, galleries and retained roof work together.
steps.prompt: Draw a longitudinal architectural section through the centre of the atrium. Show ground +0.00, level 1 +4.50, level 2 +9.00 and eaves +13.50. Retain the sawtooth roof outside the atrium. Cut the roof over the 18 m void and add a low-iron glass lantern set back 1.5 m from its edges. Show an independent dark bronze frame carrying the new lantern and gallery loads. Keep the existing brick shell separate from new steel. Add a concept-only engineering note that licensed structural and fire review is required.

steps.title: 6. Explain the assembly, not just the silhouette
steps.text: The exploded axon exposes what is retained, cut, framed and glazed.
steps.prompt: Create an exploded axonometric diagram of the factory conversion in four layers. 01 RETAIN: brick shell and cast-iron grid. 02 CUT: floor plates at levels 1 and 2, and the roof, only over bays 3–4 / B–C. 03 FRAME: independent dark bronze steel around the void. 04 LANTERN: a low-iron glazed roof set back 1.5 m. Keep the 18 × 12 m opening aligned in every layer and identify the single removed column at 4/C.

steps.title: 7. Keep the façade calm
steps.text: The new work shows at the roofline; it does not erase the industrial identity.
steps.prompt: Create a before/after north façade sheet for a red-brick 1912 textile factory. Retain the arched window rhythm and sawtooth profile. In the after view, add only a restrained glazed lantern over bays 3–4, visibly set back behind the parapet. Do not reclad the façade, add oversized signs, or replace historic windows with curtain wall. Use a clear comparison layout and label exactly what is retained and what is added.

steps.title: 8. Give materials jobs
steps.text: Brick carries history. Bronze identifies new structure. Glass delivers light. Oak and wool make the public room usable.
steps.prompt: Create a restrained material palette for an adaptive-reuse boutique hotel. Include: repaired existing red brick; dark bronze independent steel; low-iron glass; oak and moss-green wool for lounge interiors. Add one construction-facing rule: all new metal and glass stop 25–50 mm short of historic brick, creating a visible shadow gap. Use large samples, short labels and no generic trend names.

steps.title: 9. Generate one render that obeys the drawings
steps.text: The final render is a coordination check: the shell, two galleries, lifts and 18 × 12 m void must match the drawings.
steps.prompt: Deliverable: a single photorealistic architectural interior visualization, landscape 16:10. Eye-level view from the reception side into an 18 m × 12 m central atrium in a converted 1912 textile factory. Retain red brick, tall cast-iron columns and sawtooth roof profile. Add a dark bronze independent frame, two glass lift enclosures, 2.0 m galleries at levels +4.50 and +9.00, and a low-iron roof lantern set back 1.5 m from the cut roof edges. Add a quiet lounge bar with oak, moss-green wool seating, restrained plants and a few guests. Use a 35 mm lens, balanced verticals, soft overcast daylight, real material wear and physically plausible contact shadows. No signage, text, logos, neon, cyberpunk styling, marble lobby, or extra floors.

guides.result: A coordinated senior concept package: 9 linked steps, an annotated final render, SVG sources and a 9933 × 7016 px A1 presentation board. Concept study only; site survey and licensed structural, fire, access, MEP and conservation review are required before construction.

guides.title: Rebrand carousel: five jeweled brand icons with one prompt formula
guides.desc: Turn five familiar brand marks — YouTube, X, Quadcode, ChatGPT and Apple — into one luxury object series: glossy inflated metal, crystal detailing, black studio background. One reusable material formula, five swappable silhouettes.

steps.title: 1. Lock the material formula once — then only swap the silhouette
steps.text: The series works because every icon shares one physical recipe: an inflated glossy-metal body, jewel/crystal accents, a pure black studio background and controlled rim lighting. Write that recipe as a fixed block and reuse it verbatim in all five prompts — the only variables are the brand silhouette and its signature color. Icon 01 tests the formula on the YouTube play button: a rounded red jeweled slab with the triangle read as a cut gem.
steps.prompt: Premium 3D brand icon, square 1:1, luxury product photography on a pure black studio background. Subject: the YouTube play-button icon reimagined as a physical jeweled object — a rounded-square slab of glossy inflated red metal, surface like polished automotive lacquer, with the white play triangle inset as a faceted crystal gem catching the light. Fine details: soft balloon-like inflation of the edges, crisp specular highlights, subtle red light bloom on the black floor, micro-scratches absent, showroom-clean. Lighting: one key light from upper left, cool rim light from the right, controlled reflections. Tangible and physical, NOT flat vector art, NOT a UI screenshot. Hard constraints: single object centered, generous negative space, no text, no watermark, no extra logos.

steps.title: 2. X — let black-on-black carry the drama
steps.text: The hardest slide: a black object on a black background. The trick is to spell out the separation mechanism — rim light and crystal facets do all the work. Describe the mark as cut obsidian with jeweled edges so the silhouette reads purely through highlights, not through color contrast.
steps.prompt: Premium 3D brand icon, square 1:1, luxury product photography on a pure black studio background. Subject: the X (Twitter) logomark reimagined as a physical jeweled object — a bold glossy black obsidian X with beveled crystal-cut edges, like a gem carved from dark glass, faint smoky depth inside the material. Separation from the background comes entirely from bright white rim lighting tracing every edge and sharp specular sparkles on the facets. Fine details: inflated rounded body, mirror-grade polish, subtle cool reflection pooled beneath the object. Tangible and physical, NOT flat vector art. Hard constraints: single object centered, generous negative space, no text, no watermark, no extra logos.

steps.title: 3. Quadcode sparkle — the warm focal point of the set
steps.text: Every curated set needs one warm anchor. The Quadcode sparkle takes the brand gradient (#FF9569 → #DD344D) as its actual material color, so it becomes the emotional center of the carousel while still obeying the same formula: inflated gloss, crystal accents, black void around it.
steps.prompt: Premium 3D brand icon, square 1:1, luxury product photography on a pure black studio background. Subject: a four-pointed sparkle/star mark reimagined as a physical jeweled object — glossy inflated metal with a coral-to-crimson gradient finish flowing from #FF9569 at the top points to #DD344D at the base, like anodized liquid metal. A small crystal core glows softly at the center where the four points meet. Fine details: balloon-smooth inflation, razor-clean point tips, warm coral light spill on the black floor, restrained bloom. Lighting: warm key light, cool rim accents. Tangible and physical, NOT flat vector art. Hard constraints: single object centered, generous negative space, no text, no watermark, no extra logos.

steps.title: 4. ChatGPT knot — sell the geometry, not the gloss
steps.text: The knot's interlaced geometry is the whole recognition value, so the prompt protects it explicitly: 'keep every strand separate and readable'. Green gets stated as a material (jade-like metal), not a lighting gel — otherwise the model floods the whole frame green and kills the black background.
steps.prompt: Premium 3D brand icon, square 1:1, luxury product photography on a pure black studio background. Subject: the interlaced hexagonal knot mark reimagined as a physical jeweled object — six interwoven rounded strands of glossy jade-green metal, each strand inflated and balloon-smooth, weaving over and under each other with every strand separate and readable. Crystal-like highlights run along the strand curves; the weave casts soft internal shadows on itself. Fine details: showroom polish, faint green reflection beneath the object, background stays pure black. Lighting: key light from above, thin white rim light tracing the outer strands. Tangible and physical, NOT flat vector art. Hard constraints: single object centered, generous negative space, no text, no watermark, no extra logos.

steps.title: 5. Apple — close the set with restraint
steps.text: The finale goes quiet on purpose: brushed silver, minimal sparkle, maximum surface quality. After four louder objects, restraint is what makes the set read as curated instead of repetitive. Then assemble all five into one 16:10 promo banner — feed the five finished icons back into GPT-Image as references and ask for a single editorial arrangement (that's exactly how the cover of this guide was made).
steps.prompt: Premium 3D brand icon, square 1:1, luxury product photography on a pure black studio background. Subject: the Apple logomark reimagined as a physical jeweled object — glossy inflated silver metal with a soft brushed-chrome finish, the leaf as a separate polished piece with a faint crystal edge. Understated elegance: fewer sparkles than a gem, more mirror-like surface perfection, cool neutral reflections. Fine details: balloon-smooth inflation, immaculate surface, subtle silver glow pooled on the black floor. Lighting: soft key light, crisp white rim light on the silhouette. Tangible and physical, NOT flat vector art. Hard constraints: single object centered, generous negative space, no text, no watermark, no extra logos.

guides.result: Five brand marks rendered as one luxury object family — same inflated glossy-metal material, same black studio, same lighting system, five different silhouettes. Finish by compositing the five icons into a single 16:10 promo banner with GPT-Image using the icons themselves as references. Reuse the formula: keep the material block fixed, swap the silhouette, state the brand color as a material.

guides.title: Direct an epic boss-reveal cinematic shot
guides.desc: One warrior, one colossal tree-golem, a single glowing slash — build a AAA game-trailer beat in 15 seconds flat.

steps.title: 1. Design a boss silhouette you've never seen before
steps.text: Skip generic dragons. A living, cracked tree given a rough humanoid stance instantly reads as ancient and hostile without a single line of backstory — the cherry blossoms softening a threat make it feel like a cursed god of the forest, not a monster-of-the-week.
steps.prompt: A colossal ancient tree given a hulking humanoid silhouette — thick root-legs planted wide, gnarled bark skin split by glowing molten-orange cracks across its chest, branches heavy with pink cherry blossoms, a faint carved face buried in its trunk. Towering scale against a small human figure below. Cinematic realism, volumetric god-rays through blossom petals, dust and pollen drifting in the air, epic AAA game-trailer lighting.

steps.title: 2. Block the shot like a director, not a slideshow
steps.text: One continuous 15-second beat, not three cuts: open low and wide on the boss to sell scale, hold on the lone armored swordsman squaring up beneath it, then push into the exchange. Naming the camera behavior explicitly is what stops the model from defaulting to a static wide shot for the whole clip.
steps.prompt: Cinematic single continuous shot, low wide-angle framing a giant tree-golem boss against cherry blossom trees and a misty stream, warrior in white lamellar armor with twin swords standing small in the foreground. Slow creeping push-in toward the confrontation, natural handheld micro-shake, warm late-afternoon backlight, shallow depth on foreground petals, 15 seconds, no cuts.

steps.title: 3. Give the impact one clear VFX signature
steps.text: A single golden energy arc on the sword slash is the whole payoff of the shot — it needs to read instantly against the dark bark, so keep every other light source warm and secondary. One bright, legible effect beats five competing particle systems.
steps.prompt: The warrior lunges and slashes upward with a katana, leaving one bright golden energy arc trailing the blade that cracks against the tree-golem's molten chest fissure, sparks and bark fragments scattering, camera holds steady through the impact, cherry blossom petals knocked loose drifting past frame, warm rim light, no text, no logos.

steps.title: 4. Cut it, don't trim it
steps.text: Rendered clips run long and often drift in the last second or two — pick the exact in/out points where the wind-up starts and the impact settles, instead of publishing the raw output. Press play above for the final 15-second cut.

guides.result: A 15-second AAA-style boss-reveal cinematic — one creature design, one directed camera move, one clean VFX hit, no cuts needed to sell the scale.

guides.title: Retouch and color grade a product photo into a full ad set
guides.desc: Take one raw headphone photo and turn it into a commercial hero, a clean e-comm shot and a vertical detail — without killing the metal and leather textures.

steps.title: 1. Shoot (or generate) an honest raw source
steps.text: The whole exercise starts from a photo with real-world flaws — flat lighting, fingerprints and fine scratches on the metal, slight wear on the leather. Do not start from a perfect render; you need something to actually retouch. Keep materials detailed and lighting soft so you have room to push the grade later.
steps.prompt: Photorealistic product photograph of premium over-ear headphones on a clean dark studio background. Silver metal ear cups with visible fine scratches, smudges and fingerprints. Black leather ear cushions with natural texture and slight wear. Soft even studio lighting, no dramatic shadows, slightly flat color. Shot on 85mm lens, eye-level, centered composition, clean but imperfect — ready for retouch. High detail on materials, realistic reflections, no text, no logos, no watermark.

steps.title: 2. Retouch and grade the commercial hero
steps.text: This is the controlled edit — not a redesign. You remove scratches and smudges from the metal but keep it brushed and real (no plastic gloss, no chrome mirror). The leather keeps every bit of its grain; you clean dust, not texture. Then you re-light it into a premium hero and apply the cinematic grade. Reframe to 16:9 with breathing room on one side for a future headline.
steps.prompt: Retouch and re-light this exact headphone product photo into a premium commercial hero shot. Keep the same headphones, same materials, same identity — controlled edit only, no redesign. Retouch pass: remove fine scratches, smudges and fingerprints from the silver metal ear cups and yokes. Keep the metal brushed and real — no plastic gloss, no chrome mirror look. Preserve the leather grain on the headband and ear cushions exactly; clean only dust, not texture. Lighting and grade: dramatic premium studio lighting, large soft key from upper-left, cool rim light tracing the metal edges, deep charcoal background with a subtle warm gradient falloff. Rich cinematic color grade: deep blacks, lifted metal highlights, slightly warm silver tone, controlled reflections on the cups — elegant streaks, not chaos. Composition: reframe to a wide 16:9 hero crop, headphones slightly right of center with breathing room on the left for future headline text. Shot on 85mm, shallow depth of field, tack-sharp ear cups. No text, no logos, no watermark, no extra objects, no CGI plastic look.

steps.title: 3. Cut the clean e-comm catalog shot
steps.text: Same retouch rules, totally different light. Marketplaces need honesty: bright even lighting, a neutral seamless background, true-to-life color and the product centered and symmetrical. No stylized grade here — the goal is an accurate, trustworthy listing photo, not a mood piece.
steps.prompt: Retouch this exact headphone product photo into a clean e-commerce catalog shot. Same headphones, same materials, same identity — controlled edit only, no redesign. Retouch pass: remove fine scratches, smudges and fingerprints from the silver metal ear cups and yokes. Keep the metal brushed and real. Preserve leather grain on headband and ear cushions; clean only dust. Lighting and grade: bright, even, neutral catalog lighting — large soft frontal key, gentle fill, no harsh shadows, clean light-grey seamless background (#EDEDED). True-to-life color, no stylized grade: natural silver, deep natural black leather, balanced contrast for marketplaces. Composition: perfectly centered 1:1 square, headphones upright and symmetrical, generous even margins on all sides, product fills ~70% of frame height.
